text.p: Investors should hold shares in Polish tyremaker TC Debica SA, with the stock fairly valued at present while being a good long-term investment, Salomon Brothers in London said in a report.

"TC Debica is trading at a 36-percent P/E premium to the market and a 38-percent premium to its competitor Stomil Olsztyn. We believe this premium fairly reflects the company's dominant position in the Polish tyre market and rate the stock Hold," the report dated October 9 said.
Debica, which is majority-owned by Goodyear, has since risen to 64 from 61 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse. @

Salomon said a good sign for Debica was the 36-percent rise in auto sales in this year's first eight months, with industry estimates seeing 300,000 units being sold this year against 265,000 last year.

But it said that Debica's market share in passenger replacement tyres would slip to 50 or 55 percent by decade's end from the current 65 percent as Stomil, majority-owned by Michelin, expanded its production base.
Salomon predicted Debica would lift net profit to 42.2 million zlotys this year and 51.4 million zlotys next year from 35.5 million in 1995. @
It said sales would increase to 621.6 million zlotys this year and 789.5 million zlotys next year from 497.3 million zlotys in 1995.
